deck.title: Propositum 2040: Forget Utopia, Ignore Dystopia, Embrace Protopia
deck.note: Source Card #53 LORE includes malformed phrase 'bom backed backed'; edited Beat uses the corresponding intact Power clause. Do not overwrite original Card.

performance.performerCandidate: Uncle FrizzleBob, DRY solo spoken stand-up
performance.sunoStyle: Solo dry spoken-word stand-up, one clear natural storyteller voice, no singing, no music, no instrumentation, no backing track or chorus; restrained deadpan with natural 0.5–1.5 second pauses between independent Card beats and clear emphasis on each source-derived absurd consequence. Preserve every title exactly.

beats.title: The Utopian Mirage
beats.surfaceText: Ever heard of The Utopian Mirage? Skip a turn staring at the clouds and discard a resource into Dystopia; your fictional default rests on somebody else's dystopia.

beats.title: The Dystopian Apathy
beats.surfaceText: The Dystopian Apathy freezes the board for a round while you collect three profit tokens from a burning bank: a cautionary tale turned escapism and a disaster capitalism roadmap.

beats.title: The Extractive Status-Quo
beats.surfaceText: Do you know The Extractive Status-Quo? Steal 1 resource from everyone else to mitigate damage, then call the taking sustainability while the damage continues.

beats.title: The Protopian Process
beats.surfaceText: The Protopian Process says repair one broken board tile and draw a card: proactive prototyping instead of waiting, with reciprocity as the way to tackle inequities.

beats.title: The Pop Futurist
beats.surfaceText: Ever heard of The Pop Futurist? Instantly silence all critical inquiry cards, then evangelize a singular technology as a magic pill; critical inquiry would only spoil the sales pitch.

beats.title: The Academic Gatekeeper
beats.surfaceText: The Academic Gatekeeper charges an opponent from the Global South 70k tokens just to play, then says you are not a futurist unless you buy their models.

beats.title: The Tech Singularity Savior
beats.surfaceText: The Tech Singularity Savior destroys 3 worker-ants for one Tech Ego point, selling the very tech-optimism that, in this card's lore, brought us to the absolute brink.

beats.title: The Doom-Monger
beats.surfaceText: Do you know The Doom-Monger? Blast the megaphone until all players lose their next action phase; a binary collapse story does not mobilize society, it produces total inaction.

beats.title: The Disaster Capitalist
beats.surfaceText: The Disaster Capitalist gains +5 Profit whenever a fire or flood costs another player resources; the world is burning, and the card asks how much profit that suffering makes.

beats.title: The Tokenizing Crypto-Bro
beats.surfaceText: Ever heard of The Tokenizing Crypto-Bro? Convert someone else's free action into a paid micro-transaction, because apparently humans need a financial incentive even to act.

beats.title: The Philanthro-Capitalist
beats.surfaceText: The Philanthro-Capitalist manufactures 10 Toxic Waste tokens, donates one to repair a reputation score, and calls fossil fuels plus charity corporate social responsibility.

beats.title: The Air Purifier Economy
beats.surfaceText: The Air Purifier Economy says privatize the commons: pay one token every turn just to draw a card, until only the wealthy can afford to breathe.

beats.title: The Long-Termist
beats.surfaceText: Do you know The Long-Termist? Ignore present board damage while banking victory points for imaginary games a billion years away; present climate impacts can wait for imaginary lives.

beats.title: The Effective Altruist
beats.surfaceText: The Effective Altruist sacrifices a low-tier opponent card to fund AI Armageddon research, insisting that is better charity than feeding a starving child.

beats.title: The Tech Determinist
beats.surfaceText: The Tech Determinist deflects all blame because the technology wanted it; the card's lore remembers the specific humans designed it to abuse you.

beats.title: The Semantic Collapser
beats.surfaceText: Ever heard of The Semantic Collapser? Change the definition of every keyword until nothing means anything; it steals good words like long-term before anybody can argue.

beats.title: The Minority World Consumer
beats.surfaceText: The Minority World Consumer requires ten Earth board-spaces and consumes a hundred times another card's resources, while the poorest are expected to share one planet.

beats.title: The Majority World Pioneer
beats.surfaceText: The Majority World Pioneer takes 3 damage from climate impacts it did not cause and still gains a Pioneer Solution; the players who contributed the least suffer the worst.

beats.title: The Predatory Includer
beats.surfaceText: The Predatory Includer steals the aesthetic of a marginalized card to bypass corporate defenses; that becomes a new face for selling exploitative crypto to vulnerable communities.

beats.title: The Dead Voter
beats.surfaceText: Do you know The Dead Voter? Cast a vote from the discard pile that fixes today's board state for the unborn; apparently even death does not end the argument over tomorrow.

beats.title: The Disinformation Architect
beats.surfaceText: The Disinformation Architect scrambles the text on a rule card until nothing is real and everything is possible; confusion itself becomes a tool for geopolitical goals.

beats.title: The QAnon Cultist
beats.surfaceText: Ever heard of The QAnon Cultist? Build a narrative vacuum around broken systems and collect a follower for each one; the lore calls it a brand new religion.

beats.title: The Elderly Conspiracist
beats.surfaceText: The Elderly Conspiracist hands out 3 Fake News damage tokens to younger cards; the card blames weak tech literacy for making outrageous conspiracies travel so easily.

beats.title: The VR Fear-Engine
beats.surfaceText: The VR Fear-Engine triggers fear for maximum profit with zero imagination points; janky and cheap still wins if fear costs the least imagination.

beats.title: The Disability Justice Bear
beats.surfaceText: Do you know The Disability Justice Bear? Center those at the bleeding edge to prevent the next global harm card; its lore says protecting people at the edge of technological and social harm protects everyone.

beats.title: The Queer Futurist
beats.surfaceText: The Queer Futurist turns an Either/Or attack into a Plurality resource; divergent perspectives are not merely tolerated but met with actual curiosity, because plurality is survival.

beats.title: The Indigenous Wisdom Elephant
beats.surfaceText: The Indigenous Wisdom Elephant reveals the history of a stolen resource and reclaims it for the ecosystem; the lore remembers a narrative species long before that idea became a bestselling book.

beats.title: The Intersectional Octopus
beats.surfaceText: Ever heard of The Intersectional Octopus? Play 3 action cards when the water rises; lived experience on the ground beats an Ivory Tower PhD at that exact moment.

beats.title: The Homogenized Default
beats.surfaceText: The Homogenized Default replaces somebody's unique card with a blank white square, then pretends its own privileged perspective is neutral.

beats.title: The Unpaid Minority Consultant
beats.surfaceText: The Unpaid Minority Consultant decolonizes a project for 0 tokens while the Corporate Expediter takes the credit; the final product does not even name the labor.

beats.title: The Epidemic Denier
beats.surfaceText: Do you know The Epidemic Denier? Ignore pandemic damage, permanently lose all credibility, and still refuse to answer for predicting pandemics were over before COVID hit.

beats.title: The Corporate Expediter
beats.surfaceText: The Corporate Expediter sells 3 toxic assets for double profit under a green veneer; the card calls that a thin veneer of sustainability over selling more stuff.

beats.title: The Proactive Prototyper
beats.surfaceText: The Proactive Prototyper repairs a card and instantly draws another challenge; the moment anything gets fixed, the lore says there is still more to work on.

beats.title: The Regenerative Earthworm
beats.surfaceText: Ever heard of The Regenerative Earthworm? Turn toxic soil into flora by trading two Extractive damage tokens for a regenerative resource: Extractive taking versus Regenerative repair.

beats.title: Futures Literacy Library
beats.surfaceText: Futures Literacy Library removes a Conspiracy token from every elderly card by educating the board; the lore insists schools and elderly re-education both matter against the conspiracy wave.

beats.title: Radical Imagination
beats.surfaceText: Radical Imagination discards the status quo board and builds something fundamentally different from the root; its lore calls that a survival strategy, not another small tweak.

beats.title: The Interdisciplinary Weaver
beats.surfaceText: Do you know The Interdisciplinary Weaver? Connect two scientific disciplines to bypass a silo block, because the future is too complex for silos and cross-pollination is how we survive.

beats.title: The Awe & Wonder Generator
beats.surfaceText: The Awe & Wonder Generator lights up the dark until people voluntarily pay tokens to join a story; they were hungry for stories worth participating in.

beats.title: The Ministry of Stories
beats.surfaceText: The Ministry of Stories draws two cards by making climate action as addictive as doomscrolling; the aim is a meaningful story as absorbing as a QAnon wormhole.

beats.title: The Historical Bloodhound
beats.surfaceText: The Historical Bloodhound makes a Pop Futurist discard their highest-funded failure; the lore says media should hold those future-selling thought-leaders accountable.

beats.title: The Narrative Vacuum
beats.surfaceText: Ever heard of The Narrative Vacuum? Say no no no without a hopeful vision and watch nefarious actors fill the resulting power vacuum.

beats.title: The Superhero Complex
beats.surfaceText: The Superhero Complex says wait for a magical savior, do nothing, and automatically trigger Populism; the lore warns what happens when one person is supposed to save everyone.

beats.title: The Eugenic Root
beats.surfaceText: The Eugenic Root disguises racism as math and burrows into elite futurism; its lore calls out racist, ableist ideas hiding in the founders' assumptions.

beats.title: The Vaccine-Hybrid Myth
beats.surfaceText: Do you know The Vaccine-Hybrid Myth? Spread nineteenth-century paranoia that health upgrades will turn opponents into livestock; the lore recalls old vaccine fears about turning into a cow.

beats.title: The Central Banker
beats.surfaceText: The Central Banker changes behavior today by lying about what is coming tomorrow; the lore points out that predictions can change their own outcomes.

beats.title: The Expectation Setter
beats.surfaceText: The Expectation Setter holds the Overton window open so the Hope card cannot be discarded; in that open window, hope actually lives.

beats.title: The Developing Label
beats.surfaceText: The Developing Label forces another player to copy a toxic growth model; its lore objects to calling some nations finished while prescribing that same model to everyone else.

beats.title: The Magic Pill
beats.surfaceText: The Magic Pill swallows a microchip, declares a social crisis solved, and loses a turn; the lore warns that no single technology fixes deeply rooted human problems.

beats.title: The Radical Hope Activist
beats.surfaceText: Ever heard of The Radical Hope Activist? Defeat any Doomerism card and never skip your turn; in this deck, optimism takes courage and anger against apathy.

beats.title: The Plurality Hive
beats.surfaceText: The Plurality Hive combines 3 divergent cultural cards into an indestructible hive; top-up, not top-down, because divergent perspectives build better solutions.

beats.title: Accessible Scholarship
beats.surfaceText: Accessible Scholarship pays for a Global South player's flight instead of making them pay; the lore wants grants that amplify Global South voices rather than another invoice.

beats.title: The Citizen Engager
beats.surfaceText: Do you know The Citizen Engager? Move beyond the corporate realm and engage all citizens at planetary scale; the lore asks whether this is the future we actually want.

beats.title: Rule of Action
beats.surfaceText: Rule of Action bans passive play: optimism must be backed by calloused hands, and you cannot skip your turn just because pessimism feels easier.

beats.title: Rule of Plurality
beats.surfaceText: Rule of Plurality tells you to trade cards with the margins; no single player can win alone, and winning alone is a dystopian illusion.

beats.title: Rule of Repair
beats.surfaceText: Rule of Repair weaves shredded corporate documents into a nest, then makes you repair one piece of the board every draw; this game is never finished.

beats.title: Rule of Epistemic Sabotage
beats.surfaceText: Rule of Epistemic Sabotage says flip the table whenever the rules favor the extractive player and rewrite them; its lore repeats the demand: rewrite the rules.
